desk.headline: Normalised continuing HEPS up 10.5% to 2,087c on 4.5% volume growth; reported revenue flat at R34.2bn; final dividend up 5.7%; margin and ROIC targets raised
results: Normalised continuing HEPS rose 10.5% to 2,087c; total-operations HEPS rose 5.2% to 2,162c, but reported continuing HEPS fell 2.5% because last year included gains tied to the Carozzi stake.
Reported revenue slipped 0.5% to R34.2bn as businesses were sold; on a like-for-like basis revenue grew 3.3% to R33.4bn, with volumes up 4.5% and prices down 1.2%.
Operating income grew 12.6% to R4.3bn and the operating margin widened to 12.6% from 11.1%, helped by a higher gross margin.
Grains led the gains (operating income up 52.9% to R1.1bn) and Culinary grew 17.7% to R1.3bn; Home and Personal Care was the weak spot, with operating income down 24.0% to R400m.
Capex rose to R1.7bn and the group moved to net debt of R472m from net cash of R4.49bn; the Beacon property sale added a net profit of R121m.

guidance.summary: Tiger expects FY2027 to stay tough, citing stretched consumers, supply-chain disruption and climate events. It raised its short-to-medium-term operating margin and ROIC targets and tightened its working capital target, while keeping volume growth guidance at 1-3%.

points: CEO Tjaart Kruger said pushing up prices at the cost of volume is no longer a workable way to grow; the focus is on affordability and volume.
He said national protest action disrupted the general trade channel and led to heavy de-stocking.
Higher fuel prices added cost pressure, partly offset by logistics savings, and exports benefited from steadier product supply.
Fixing the Ingram's business in Home and Personal Care and rolling out bakery digitalisation are FY2027 priorities.
CFO Thushen Govender highlighted cash generation, pointing to 94% adjusted cash conversion.
call.source: The National (26 Nov 2026) and Investing.com (26 Nov 2026) coverage of the results and presentation

watch: Whether volume growth holds up as consumer budgets stay under pressure in FY2027.
A turnaround in Home and Personal Care, where profit fell 24%.
Completion of the Chococam sale, which awaits a tax clearance and is targeted by the end of 2027.
